findings.problem: The proof requires only an existential-function test presentation of Q, not arithmeticity itself. It converts hQ to HasTest Q at line 18 and subsequently uses only that presentation. Requiring Arith Q excludes predicates supplied directly in the existing, more general test normal form.
findings.proposed_change:
Extract a generalized theorem with statement:

theorem sourceT_exists_test_real (M : ZFSet.{u}) (hM : Transitive M) (hT : SourceT M)
    {Q : Predicate} (hQ : HasTest Q) (A R : Oracle)
    (hA : A ∈ modelReals M) (hR : R ∈ modelReals M) (v : ℕ) :
    (∃ H : Oracle, Q (parameters A R H) v) ↔
      ∃ H ∈ modelReals M, Q (parameters A R H) v

The existing proof works by replacing line 18 with `obtain ⟨t,ht⟩ := hQ`; subsequent descent lemmas accept arbitrary Test values. Retain the arithmetic theorem as a corollary using `(arithmetic_tests hQ).1`. Keep the model and parameter-membership assumptions unchanged. False predicates cause no difficulty: the forward implication has no witness, and the reverse implication remains immediate.
findings.benefit: Users can transfer witnesses for predicates already expressed as existence of a function satisfying finite tests, without proving those predicates arithmetic or repeating the descent argument. Existing arithmetic callers retain their current interface.

evidence.excerpt: def HasTest (P : Predicate) : Prop := ∃ t : Test, t.Presents P

def Presents (t : Test) (P : Predicate) : Prop :=
  ∀ O v, P O v ↔ ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ n, t.eval O f (Nat.pair v n)
theorem arithmetic_tests {P} (h : Arith P) : HasTest P ∧ HasTest (fun O v => ¬ P O v) := by
